problem: Programming tools gave little real-time feedback about running code. Light Table offered an IDE that shows live results; Eve aimed to bring computation to people who are not professional programmers.
business_model: Open-source developer tool funded by crowdfunding and venture seed capital; no revenue model established in sources
product_category: Developer tools, IDE and programming environment

founders.name: Chris Granger
prior_employers: Microsoft Visual Studio team (his launch post says Visual Studio team; Microsoft not named in it)
founders.background_notes: Launch post 2012-04-12 says he worked on the Visual Studio team.

founders.name: Rob Attorri
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him co-founder of Light Table and Eve and a former research scientist.

exit.reason: Team said they could not find a good home for Eve despite leads and meetings, and began winding down the company.

competitors.name: Visual Studio
competitors.what: Mainstream window-based IDE criticized in the launch post

competitors.name: Code Bubbles
competitors.what: Earlier research spatial workspace IDE, cited as not going far enough

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a live-evaluating IDE on ClojureScript and CodeMirror was hard for a tiny team; Eve required a new language and runtime.

defensibility.rationale: Open sourced in 2014 and the ideas were public; no revenue lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it wholesale; a community kept Light Table going after the company moved on, and Eve found no acquirer by 2018.

market_need_then: Strong developer interest: the Kickstarter goal of 200K was exceeded in 2012 and the concept post drew wide discussion, though some critics said it ignored what modern IDEs already did.

branding.name_origin: Named after the engineering light table device that lets you see pictures and blueprints side by side, overlapping and interacting, per co-creator Rob Attorri as quoted by Wikipedia.
branding.domain_note: Company site was kodowa.com; sources do not give domain history.
branding.brand_signature: Light Table as a recognized name in the Clojure and live-programming community

rebrands.why: Company moved focus to a new programming environment for non-programmers, with Light Table continuing

branding.community_and_virality: Active open-source community with 100+ plugins, a mailing list and IRC, per Wikipedia summary.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known among developers after a funded Kickstarter and open-source community, but the company name Kodowa was little known and the Eve brand never shipped widely.

pivots.to: Eve, a programming environment for non-programmers
pivots.why: Stated aim to bring the ideas of Light Table to far more people

outcome_analysis: Light Table raised over 300K on Kickstarter in 2012 and built a loyal developer community, then open sourced the editor and moved to Eve with a 2.3M seed led by Andreessen Horowitz in 2014. Eve never shipped a hosted product and in January 2018 the team wound down after failing to find an acquirer. The sources do not state revenue, so the failure rests on a pivot that did not find a paying market.
notes: kodowa.com returned HTTP 503 when fetched. Kickstarter total is 300K to 316,720 per search snippets of Slashdot and others (not opened in full). CB Insights lists 330K total with a YC seed of about 20K dated 2012-06; unverified single database. The 2.3M seed rests on the founder's own post only. Chris Granger is named on the YC page as Founder and in the launch post; Granger's post of 2014-10 says three founders so far without naming the third. The YC page says Eve; Light Table the project was not shut down with the company.
